questions.q: You run zudojs generate dto coupons from shop-api/src/routes. shop-api has a .zudojs/manifest.json. Where does the DTO file go?
questions.explain: The CLI walks up from the current folder to the first folder that records a ZudoJS project, and writes relative to that root. It even prints Project root: … when the root is not the current folder.
options: shop-api/src/dtos/coupons.dto.ts, relative to the project root it found by walking up
Nowhere: the command must be run from the project root

questions.q: A folder has a package.json without a zudojs block, no .zudojs/manifest.json and no zudojs.config file. What does zudojs build do there (assuming no parent folder is a ZudoJS project)?
questions.explain: A bare package.json only proves "some JavaScript project". Accepting it once made zudojs build run an unrelated project's build script, so the CLI now requires a real ZudoJS record.
options: Runs that package's build script, since it is a Node.js project
Refuses with "This command must be run inside a Zudojs project directory."
Creates a manifest and then builds

questions.q: Which exit code does zudojs generate resource (no name) end with?
questions.explain: An incomplete command line ends with 2 and the message Missing required argument "name". Code 1 is for a command that ran and failed, 3 for an unknown command.

questions.q: A CI script runs zudojs deploy. What happens?
questions.explain: The CLI has seven commands and deploy is not one of them. Deployment is your own pipeline's job, built from npm run build and npm start.
options: It deploys using the Dockerfile from zudojs add docker
It prints Command "deploy" was not found. and exits with 3

questions.q: zudojs doctor prints two ⚠ warnings (no lock file, node_modules missing) and no ✖. What is its exit code, and what does that mean for a CI step that runs it?
questions.explain: Only ✖ errors make doctor exit with 1; it even ends with "All checks passed!" after warnings. If warnings matter in your pipeline, you must check for them explicitly.
options: 0: warnings do not fail the step, so read them yourself
2: warnings count as an incomplete setup
It depends on the package manager

questions.q: Which schematics both write a routes file and edit src/routes/index.ts and src/container.ts, so the endpoint is reachable straight away?
questions.explain: resource (with a test) and route (without one) wire the routes and the controller in. controller, service, repository and dto only write files.

questions.q: What does zudojs generate controller invoices write in a monolith?
questions.explain: Layered schematics cascade: a controller needs a service, which needs a repository, which needs the DTO types. None of them wires anything in, so the controller is not reachable until you add a route.
options: The controller and a routes file
The DTO, repository, service and controller, and it edits no existing file
A full resource with a test

questions.q: You already generated resource order-items. What does zudojs generate resource OrderItems do?
questions.explain: Names are normalized to kebab-case before anything else, so OrderItems, Order_Items and order-items are the same resource. Without --force, an existing resource is refused.
options: Creates OrderItems.controller.ts next to the old files
Refuses: it normalizes to order-items, whose files already exist

questions.q: Why does the CLI refuse zudojs generate resource records?
questions.explain: The singular of the name becomes the record type. Record, Promise, Map and other globals are refused because the generated code relies on them.
options: Resource names may not end in "s"
Its record type would be called Record, hiding TypeScript's built-in Record<K, V> in the generated files
A resource called records already exists in every project

questions.q: Why is 2fa refused as a resource name, and what does the CLI suggest?
questions.explain: A TypeScript identifier cannot start with a digit. Refusing up front is better than generating files that do not compile, and the message says what to type instead.
options: Digits are never allowed; it suggests fa
The name becomes a class name and 2faController is not a valid identifier; it suggests two-factor-auth
It is too short; it suggests 2fa-items
It is reserved for the auth package; it suggests otp

questions.q: Someone deleted the // zudojs:routes:start and …:end comments from src/routes/index.ts. What does zudojs generate resource orders do?
questions.explain: Without markers the CLI refuses to guess where the line belongs. It still generates everything else and only warns, so the route answers 404 until you add the printed line yourself.
options: Fails with exit code 1 and writes nothing
Appends the registration at the end of the file
Writes the resource files, leaves src/routes/index.ts unchanged, prints "Finish by hand" and exits with 0
Recreates the markers and inserts the line

questions.q: Marker insertion is idempotent. What does that mean in practice?
questions.explain: Before inserting, the CLI checks whether the line is already between the markers and reports present if so. Regenerating is therefore safe for the wiring.
options: It runs in the same amount of time for any file size
Running the same insertion twice leaves the file as after the first run, so --force does not register routes twice
It can be undone with git restore

questions.q: What is the main risk of zudojs generate resource products --force on an existing resource?
questions.explain: --force rewrites the schematic's files. The wiring is safe because insertion is idempotent, but your edits to the DTO, service or controller are gone. Commit first and review with git diff.
options: It registers the routes a second time
It overwrites the resource's own files, losing every hand edit in them

questions.q: A refused generate ("already exists") leaves no new files behind. Which design makes that true?
questions.explain: Plan, check, then write. Checking file by file while writing would leave a half-generated resource when the third file clashes.
options: It writes to a temporary folder and renames it
It builds the full list of files first, checks the whole list against the disk, and writes only if nothing clashes
It deletes what it wrote when it hits a clash
It writes the files in alphabetical order

questions.q: In a modular monolith you run zudojs generate service refunds --module billing. What does the published CLI do?
questions.explain: In a modular monolith the CLI treats "service" as "module". To get a service inside billing, generate a resource or controller with --module billing and keep the layers you need.
options: Refuses, because services cannot live in modules
Prints Mapping "service" → "module" and creates a new module called refunds, ignoring --module billing
Creates a service in the shared src/services folder

questions.q: A modular monolith already has a top-level invoices resource. Why is zudojs generate resource invoices --module billing refused?
questions.explain: Source files go to src/modules/billing/…, but tests are not grouped by module. The only clash was tests/invoices.test.ts.
options: Module resources must have unique class names across the app
Its test would also be tests/invoices.test.ts, which already exists
The billing module does not allow resources

questions.q: In a microservice project, where does zudojs generate resource refunds (run from the project root, no --service) put the files?
questions.explain: Without --service the gateway is the target. --service payments targets apps/services/payments/, and an unknown service name is refused.

questions.q: Why is the file written by zudojs generate validator payment dangerous if left as it is?
questions.explain: The stub compiles and accepts everything, including "DROP TABLE". Replace its body with a real schema check and add a test with bad input before anything calls it.
options: validatePayment returns true for any input, yet its name suggests it checks something
It sends payments to a test provider

questions.q: Your team wants its own zudojs generate webhook schematic. What does the published CLI offer?
questions.explain: The templates are built into the CLI and cannot be extended. The zudojs-cli package does export the CLI framework (createCLI), so project-specific commands are easy to write.
options: A templates/ folder in the project that it reads automatically
No custom schematics; generate the closest one and edit it, or build your own commands with createCLI from zudojs-cli

questions.q: A CI job runs npx zudojs@latest generate …. What problem can that cause?
questions.explain: Pin the version (npx zudojs@2.1.3) so every developer and every pipeline run uses the same templates, and upgrade on purpose.
options: A new CLI release can change the generated code without any change in your repository

questions.q: After zudojs add database, you generate resource coupons. The project already had a products resource. Which repositories does src/container.ts build?
questions.explain: The CLI changes templates for resources generated from then on, and says so. Existing resources keep their in-memory repository until you swap it in src/container.ts. The service does not change because it only knows the repository interface.
options: A Prisma repository for coupons; products keeps its in-memory repository
In-memory repositories for both until you run db:migrate
Neither: the database feature removes the container

questions.q: A monolith made by create loses both its manifest and its zudojs block, but keeps a zudojs.config.ts with no architecture. Which architecture does the fallback guess?
questions.explain: The folder heuristics say "src/modules means modular monolith", and a generated monolith has that folder too. That is why the recorded architecture must be kept.
options: monolith, because that is the default
modular-monolith, because the project has a src/modules folder

questions.q: What does zudojs dev -p 4100 do in a backend project?
questions.explain: dev hands the work to your dev script and passes the port as PORT, which src/configs/index.ts reads. No file is changed.
options: Runs npm run dev with the PORT environment variable set to 4100
Starts a proxy on 4100 in front of port 3000
Nothing: -p only works in full-stack projects

questions.q: What does zudojs create shop --language javascript give you for a backend?
questions.explain: The option appears in the help, but it applies to frontends. For --type backend the CLI prints that JavaScript is not supported.
options: A JavaScript backend with JSDoc types
Nothing: it refuses, because backend projects are TypeScript only

questions.q: What does this print?
questions.explain: A dash goes between a lowercase letter and a capital, and between an acronym and the next word (HTTP + Logs). Everything else that is not a letter, digit or dash becomes a dash, and dashes at the ends are trimmed.

questions.q: What does this print?
questions.explain: The rules are simple English, not a dictionary. deliveries and branches come out right, but news loses its final s and so does status, because the letter before the s is not another s. Check the singular the CLI will derive before you name a resource, or pick a name with a regular plural.

questions.q: What does this print?
questions.explain: The first call adds the line between the markers (three lines now). The second finds the same line already there and changes nothing, so the file still has three lines. That is idempotency.

questions.q: What does this print?
questions.explain: The end marker must come after the start marker, and the names must match exactly: containers is not container. In each failing case the CLI would leave the file unchanged and print "Finish by hand".

questions.q: Here the file system is a set of paths. What does this print?
questions.explain: The walk goes up from /code/shop/src/routes until it finds the manifest in /code/shop. /code/blog only has a package.json, which this check does not accept, so the walk reaches / and returns null.

questions.q: What does this print?
questions.explain: Without a record, a workspace file alone is not enough for "microservice" (there is no apps/gateway), so src/modules decides. A recorded architecture always wins over guessing.

questions.q: What does this print?
questions.explain: The whole plan is checked first, so the refused run adds nothing (still 1 file). With force, all three paths are added; the service path was already there, so the set holds 3.

questions.q: What does this print?
questions.explain: This is the comparison behind doctor's Capabilities check: each list is checked against the other, and events is in both.
options: manifest only: openapi; package.json only: cqrs
manifest only: openapi,events; package.json only: events,cqrs
manifest only: cqrs; package.json only: openapi

questions.q: What does this print?
questions.explain: Files and URLs keep the kebab-case slug; classes join the capitalised parts. One slug, several spellings, all derived by fixed rules.

questions.q: Each pair is a step name and its exit code. What does this print?
questions.explain: The failing step still runs (and is recorded); the loop stops after it, so test never runs. Real CI stops the same way on the first non-zero exit code.
options: doctor > typecheck > build > test | result: fail
doctor > typecheck > build > test | result: pass

questions.q: What does this print?
questions.explain: The generated stub accepts every input, including a negative amount and null. That is why stubs must be replaced before anything relies on them.

questions.q: What does this print?
questions.explain: The URL uses the plural slug; the record type uses the singular. ies becomes y.

questions.q: Write normalizeName(name) that turns a typed name into the CLI's kebab-case slug: split camelCase and acronyms, lowercase, turn any run of other characters into one dash, and trim dashes at both ends.
questions.explain: Split before lowercasing, or the case information is lost. The second replace handles acronyms: HTTPServer becomes HTTP-Server, not H-T-T-P-Server.

questions.q: Write singularize(slug): ies → y (for words longer than 4 letters), drop es after s, x, z, ch or sh, otherwise drop a final s unless the word ends in ss.
questions.explain: Order the rules from most to least specific: ies first, then the es endings, then a plain s. glass ends in ss, so it is left alone.

questions.q: Write insertLine(source, name, line): insert line just before // zudojs:NAME:end (on its own line, with the same indentation as the end marker), unless it is already between the markers. Return the new source, or throw Error("missing markers") if the markers are missing or in the wrong order.
questions.explain: The indentation is whatever sits between the start of the end marker's line and the marker. Checking for the line first makes the function idempotent, so the second call changes nothing.

questions.q: Write findRoot(start, markers). markers is a Set of folders that contain a project record. Walk up from start (paths use /) and return the first folder in the set, or null after checking /.
questions.explain: The nearest record wins, which is why running the CLI inside a microservice's service folder treats that service as the project. The || "/" handles the step from /work to the top.

questions.q: Write checkResourceName(slug, entity) that returns "ok", or an error text: "paths are not allowed" if the slug contains / or .., "must start with a letter" if it starts with a digit, and "ENTITY would shadow a global" if the entity is Record, Promise or Map.
questions.explain: Validate the input before it becomes a path or an identifier. Checking the path first matters: a name like ../2fa should be reported as a path, the more dangerous mistake.
questions.expected:
ok
paths are not allowed
must start with a letter
Record would shadow a global

questions.q: Write compareCapabilities(manifestList, featureList). Return "same" when both hold the same names in any order, otherwise a line for each name found in only one list, like "openapi: manifest only", joined with "; ". Manifest-only names come first.
questions.explain: Two records of one fact drift apart, so something must compare them in both directions. Sets make "is it in the other list" a quick lookup.
questions.expected:
same
openapi: manifest only; queue: package.json only

questions.q: Write runSteps(steps). Each step is { name, code }. Print NAME: ok for code 0; on the first non-zero code print NAME: failed (exit CODE), skip the rest, and return that code. Return 0 when every step passes.
questions.explain: Returning the failing code, instead of a generic 1, keeps the information a caller needs: a 2 means "your command line is wrong", a 1 "the work failed".
questions.expected:
doctor: ok
build: failed (exit 1)
result 1
typecheck: ok
result 0

questions.q: Write parseArgs(argv) for a tiny project CLI. The first word is the command, other plain words are arguments, and --name value pairs are options. Convert an option value to a number when Number(value) is finite.
questions.explain: This is the job createCLI from zudojs-cli does for you, plus help, required arguments and exit codes. Writing it once shows why you would rather not maintain your own.
